_comment: Pre-arrival immigration/customs forms per destination, keyed by ISO-2 country code. Hand-curated and verified against official government sites — incomplete by design, like data/passport-index.json's VISA_PORTAL. window = how long before arrival it can/must be submitted. mandatory = false means it's only required if you have something to declare, or optional-but-recommended for faster clearance.

TH.name: Thailand Digital Arrival Card (TDAC)
TH.notes: Replaced the paper TM6 card in May 2025. Single entry only — resubmit each time you cross the border. Watch for fake lookalike sites that charge a fee; the real one is free.

MY.name: Malaysia Digital Arrival Card (MDAC)
MY.notes: Mandatory for most foreign visitors since Jan 2024. Free — ignore third-party sites charging up to $80.

SG.name: SG Arrival Card (SGAC)
SG.window: within 3 days before arrival (incl. day of arrival)
SG.notes: Also available via the MyICA app. Free.

PH.name: Philippines eTravel
PH.notes: Single platform for both arrival and departure, covers customs, health and immigration data. Free, ~10 minutes.

NZ.name: New Zealand Traveller Declaration (NZTD)
NZ.notes: Combines customs, immigration and biosecurity declarations. Required even for NZ passport holders. Free.

IN.name: Indian Customs Declaration (Atithi app)
IN.window: in advance of arrival, via app or web
IN.notes: Only needed if you're carrying dutiable goods, high-value items, or currency above the declarable limit — lets you pre-file and use the red channel faster.

ID.name: Indonesia Electronic Customs Declaration (e-CD)
ID.notes: Mandatory for all international arrivals; produces a QR code for customs.

JP.name: Visit Japan Web
JP.notes: Not strictly required (paper forms still accepted) but combines immigration (disembarkation card), customs declaration and quarantine into one QR code, saving significant airport time.

MV.name: Maldives Traveller Declaration (IMUGA)
MV.notes: Required for every foreign arrival. Free — beware paid third-party imitators.

TW.name: Taiwan Arrival Card (TWAC)
TW.notes: Replaced all paper arrival cards from Oct 1, 2025. Free; a confirmation email is sent on submission.

MX.name: Forma Migratoria Múltiple (FMM)
MX.notes: Tourist card issued by Mexico's immigration institute (INM); required for most visitors arriving by air or land.

BR.name: e-DBV (Declaração de Bens de Viajante)
BR.notes: Only required if carrying goods to declare — high-value items, electronics for resale, or cash over the legal limit.

CL.name: Chile Customs Affidavit (Declaración Jurada / SAG)
CL.notes: Declares food, plant/animal products, and currency over US$10,000. Presented to a SAG officer on arrival.

AU.name: Australia Travel Declaration (ATD)
AU.window: up to 72 hours before your flight
AU.notes: Digital replacement for the paper Incoming Passenger Card, rolling out airport-by-airport through 2026–2028 — check whether your arrival airport has switched over; the paper card is still used everywhere else.

CU.name: D'Viajeros
CU.window: from 7 days up to 48 hours before arrival
CU.notes: Single digital form replacing Cuba's old embarkation/disembarkation card, customs declaration and health affidavit. Available in English.

KR.name: Korea e-Arrival Card
KR.notes: Required for short-term foreign visitors. Customs declaration is only needed on top of this if you have goods to declare.
